name: unexpected lab result overview
title: Unexpected lab result decision chart: check pre-analytical, analytical and post-analytical error in order before believing it, each with its sources, an example and what to do; if no error is found the result may be correct and is communicated to the patient; consent before the test, confidentiality after

root.title: A lab result that doesn't fit: an ERROR, or REAL?
lines: 1 · Understand the issue: inconsistent with RELATED tests, PREVIOUS values, or the PRESENTATION?
do NOT diagnose or treat on a questionable result
before ANY test, valid consent: CAPACITY (not age) · INFORMED of benefits, risks, alternatives · VOLUNTARY

groups.title: ERROR? Check each phase IN ORDER
lines: then 5 · ask a lab professional · 6 · repeat or use a different method (Choosing Wisely)

head: h
Pre-analytical
the MOST COMMON source
src: • wrong test, wrong tube or order of draw
eg: Potassium 6.8 by pneumatic tube in leukemia, NORMAL electrocardiogram
act: Collect a fresh sample and repeat

head: h
Analytical
less frequent as technology improves
eg: different METHODS + reference intervals: not comparable
act: • other tests to rule in or out
• another method, here or another lab

head: h
Post-analytical
HUMAN error in reporting
act: right patient, right number, right reference interval

head: h
A REAL result
still be cautious
src: think of it when the result contradicts your diagnosis
eg: interpret, explain, show the Framingham risk
act: Share ONLY with the patient's consent
not the family · MUST report: a child in need of protection, or likely serious harm to others
